message.content:
Below is an overview of the key traffic laws and regulations that apply in Texas. For the most up‑to‑date and detailed information, you should consult the Texas Transportation Code, the Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS), or a qualified attorney. --- ## 1. Governing Documents | Document | What it Covers | Where to Find | |----------|----------------|---------------| | **Texas Transportation Code** | All state traffic laws, including speed limits, seat‑belt requirements, DUI rules, and vehicle registration | Texas Legislature Online (https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/) | | **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** | Driver licensing, vehicle registration, enforcement policies | https://www.dps.texas.gov/ | | **Texas Highway Patrol** | Enforcement of traffic laws on state highways | https://www.txdhhs.gov/ | --- ## 2. Major Traffic Law Topics | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No‑limit” roads exist in some rural areas.
• Speed limits are enforced by the Texas Highway Patrol and local police. | | **Seat‑Belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat.
• Failure to buckle up can result in a fine and points on your license. | | **DUI / DWI** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) limit is 0.08% for drivers over 21.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02%).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory alcohol education, and possible jail time. | | **Cell Phone Use** | • Hand‑held cell phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles approaching from the right have priority.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red lights mean stop; green means go; yellow means prepare to stop.
• Stop signs require a full stop. | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Vehicles must be registered with the DPS and carry proof of insurance.
• Failure to register or insure can lead to fines and impoundment. | | **Parking Regulations** | • Parking in no‑parking zones, fire lanes, or handicap spaces without proper permits is illegal. | | **School Bus Laws** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children. | | **Lane Usage** | • Lane usage rules (e.g., passing on the right is prohibited on two‑lane roads). | --- ## 3. Common Violations & Penalties | Violation | Typical Penalty | |-----------|-----------------| | Speeding (up to 20 mph over limit) | Fine $100–$200, 1–3 points | | Speeding (over 20 mph) | Fine $200–$500, 3–5 points | | Seat‑belt non‑use | Fine $50–$100, 1 point | | DUI (BAC 0.08–0.15) | Fine $500–$1,000, 3–5 points, 30–90 days license suspension | | Cell phone use | Fine $50–$100, 1 point | | Failure to register | Fine $100–$300, vehicle impoundment | *Points are added to your Texas driver’s license. Accumulating 12 points within 36 months can lead to license suspension.* --- ## 4. How to Check Your Points 1. Visit the Texas DPS website. 2. Log in to your account or use the “Check My Points” service. 3. Review your current point total and any pending violations. --- ## 5. Resources for More Information | Resource | Description | |----------|-------------| | **Texas Transportation Code** | Full legal text of all traffic laws. | | **Texas DPS Driver Handbook** | Practical guide for drivers, including rules and safety tips. | | **Texas Highway Patrol** | Contact information for reporting violations or seeking clarification. | | **Legal Aid & Attorneys** | If you’re facing a traffic ticket or DUI charge, consult a licensed Texas attorney. | --- ### Quick Tips - **Always obey posted speed limits** – they are set for safety and may vary by road type. - **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk on the phone. - **Keep your registration and insurance documents in the vehicle** – you’ll need them if pulled over. - **Check your points regularly** to avoid unexpected license suspensions. If you have a specific question about a particular law or situation, feel free to ask!
